memory_update.text: Use KLAC as the benchmark reference leader for process control, inspection, metrology, reticle, packaging and PCB inspection exposure.
ONTO, FORM and CAMT form a credible underfollowed direct-exposure lane for advanced packaging, metrology/inspection, HBM test and wafer-level process-control beneficiaries.

PDF Solutions should be examined in a later pass as a possible yield-management software/data candidate, but it was excluded here to keep Layer 1B capped at four companies and focused on direct equipment/test exposure.
The strongest node hypothesis to verify next is whether AI-driven HBM, chiplet and advanced-packaging complexity increases inspection/test/metrology intensity faster than overall semiconductor capex.

KLAC should remain the reference anchor for process control, inspection, metrology, reticle/mask, packaging, PCB, and yield-management exposure, but it should not dominate the discovery lane because it is already high-attention.

ONTO is a strong underfollowed-lane candidate for advanced-packaging inspection, 3D metrology, lithography, and factory analytics; next layer should verify advanced-packaging revenue mix and AI/HBM customer pull.

CAMT is a focused Nasdaq-listed advanced-packaging inspection/metrology supplier with apparent HBM and OSAT relevance; verify customer concentration, order durability, and whether demand is AI/HBM-specific.

FORM belongs in the adjacent chokepoint lane because HBM and advanced packaging increase known-good-die and wafer-test complexity; verify HBM probe-card revenue and recurrence before promoting beyond Layer 1.

This pass did not fully cover reticle-inspection pure plays, IC-substrate inspection suppliers, PCB inspection vendors, or yield-management software specialists. Later searches should test NVMI, AEIS, COHU, TER, VECO, ACLS, and non-U.S. listed niche vendors if allowed.

KLA should remain the reference anchor for semiconductor process control, inspection, metrology, reticle inspection, packaging inspection, PCB inspection, and yield management, but it is not the main underfollowed discovery target.
Onto Innovation is a credible underfollowed-lane candidate for advanced-packaging inspection/metrology, process-control analytics, and backend/package-oriented yield workflows.
Camtek is a credible underfollowed-lane candidate with direct inspection/metrology exposure to advanced packaging, OSATs, memory, and HBM-related order flow.
FormFactor is a second-order node candidate: probe cards and wafer-level test are adjacent to inspection/metrology because HBM and advanced packaging increase test intensity and yield-learning value.
Later layers should test whether these candidates are truly undercovered versus already priced by the market, especially because ONTO, CAMT, and FORM have grown beyond classic small-cap ranges.

The node should be tracked as a multi-subsegment basket: front-end process control, reticle inspection, wafer/package inspection, advanced-packaging metrology, PCB/substrate inspection, probe cards, wafer test, and yield analytics software.
KLA should remain the reference anchor for the process-control / inspection / metrology node, but not dominate the discovery lane because it is already a well-known leader.
Onto Innovation is a strong underfollowed candidate for AI-related advanced packaging inspection, 3D metrology, lithography, process-control software, and factory analytics exposure.
Camtek is a focused underfollowed candidate for advanced packaging and HBM-adjacent inspection/metrology, especially if recent OSAT/HBM order momentum is confirmed in filings.
FormFactor is a lower-attention probe-card/test-interface candidate tied to HBM and advanced-package yield validation; key risk is memory-cycle volatility and customer concentration.

Next Layer 2 work should verify revenue mix, customer concentration, backlog durability, market share, and whether each underfollowed name has incremental AI/HBM/advanced-packaging exposure not already priced into estimates.
